correctness.rationale: For \(F(x)=J(\sigma(x),x)\), linear isometry of \(J\) gives the exact formula \(\|F(x)-F(y)\|=\max\{|\sigma(x)-\sigma(y)|,\|x-y\|\}\). Hence no pair contracts. Choosing opposite selector values along a sequence converging on the sphere makes image distance exactly \(2\) while source distance tends to \(0\). This proves non-strong plasticity and forces the strong-plasticity modulus to be \(0\) for every \(0<\varepsilon<2\). Coordinate prepending verifies the hypothesis for both \(c\) and \(\ell_\infty\). No empirical step is used.

value.rationale: The result gives a reusable structural obstruction rather than an isolated counterexample: max-summand self-similarity forces the exact strong-plasticity modulus to vanish on the whole nontrivial interval. Applied to the two sup-norm sequence spheres that the focal paper newly proves plastic, it sharply separates ordinary from strong plasticity and shows the failure is maximal at arbitrarily small scales. This directly resolves a natural stronger-property question created by the focal paper’s Hilbert-versus-sup-norm comparison.
